A COUNTEREXAMPLE TO ERDŐS PROBLEM 108
VIA ARC GRAPHS
JENSEN KOHLMEYER AND LIAM KRUER
ABSTRACT. For every positive integer 𝑀, we construct a finite triangle-free graph 𝐺 with 𝜒(𝐺) ≥ 𝑀 such
that every ordinary subgraph of 𝐺 containing no four-cycle is 6-colorable. Consequently, no chromatic
threshold forces a subgraph of girth at least five and chromatic number at least seven. This gives a negative
answer to Erdős problem 108.
The proof combines two ingredients. First, a four-cycle-free subgraph of an arc graph can be parti-
tioned into a part controlled by a bounded-degree subgraph of the underlying graph and a forest. Second, a
multipartite random construction gives graphs of large chromatic number for which every bounded-degree
subgraph is 4-colorable, while retaining an acyclic orientation whose outdegree bound is independent of the
prescribed degree cap. We give explicit integer part sizes and finite probability estimates. The main theo-
rem and the negation of the pinned Formal Conjectures statement are also proved in Lean 4; the verification
uses only the permitted standard axioms.
1. INTRODUCTION
The high-girth subgraph problem of Erdős and Hajnal asks whether, for every pair of integers 𝑟 ≥ 4
and 𝑘 ≥ 2, there is an integer 𝑓 (𝑘, 𝑟 ) such that every graph of chromatic number at least 𝑓 (𝑘, 𝑟 ) contains
a subgraph of girth at least 𝑟 and chromatic number at least 𝑘. The question appears as Problem 108 in
Bloom’s catalogue [ 1] and is formalized in the Formal Conjectures library [ 2].
Throughout this paper, a subgraph may be obtained by deleting vertices and edges. In particular, “four-
cycle-free” excludes a copy of 𝐶4 as an ordinary subgraph; a four-cycle with chords is still forbidden.
Theorem 1.1. For every integer 𝑀 ≥ 1, there is a finite nonempty triangle-free simple graph 𝐺 such
that 𝜒(𝐺) ≥ 𝑀 and every four-cycle-free subgraph 𝐻 of 𝐺 satisfies 𝜒(𝐻) ≤ 6.
Corollary 1.2. There is no integer 𝑓 such that every graph of chromatic number at least 𝑓 contains a
subgraph of girth at least five and chromatic number at least seven. In particular, the assertion in Erdős
problem 108 is false.
Proof. Given a proposed threshold 𝑓 , apply Theorem 1.1 with 𝑀 = max{ 1, 𝑓 } . Every subgraph of girth
at least five is four-cycle-free, so its chromatic number is at most six. □
The construction starts with the multipartite random model used by Janzer, Steiner and Sudakov in
their work on chromatic number and regular subgraphs [ 3]. We adapt its separated-part-size method to
obtain a statement with two independent parameters: a chromatic parameter 𝑞 and a degree cap 𝐾. The
outdegree bound depends only on 𝑞. This permits us to choose 𝐾 after fixing that bound and then apply
an arc-graph argument. All estimates needed for this adaptation are proved here; the result is not used
as a consequence of the regular-subgraph theorem.
Section 2 gives the arc-graph lemmas. Section 3 constructs the base graph, including the size estimates
and both probability bounds. Section 4 proves Theorem 1.1. Section 5 describes the formal statements
and the local verification record.

2. ARC GRAPHS AND BOUNDED-DEGREE SELECTIONS
Definition 2.1. Let 𝐷 be an acyclic orientation of a simple graph. Its arc graph 𝐿(𝐷) has the arcs of 𝐷
as vertices, with two vertices adjacent precisely when the corresponding arcs concatenate. Thus (𝑢, 𝑣)
and (𝑣, 𝑤) are adjacent. We orient this edge from (𝑢, 𝑣) to (𝑣, 𝑤).
Fix a topological ordering of 𝐷. Along every oriented edge of 𝐿(𝐷), the tail of the corresponding arc
strictly increases in this ordering. The displayed orientation of 𝐿(𝐷) is therefore acyclic.
Lemma 2.2. The graph 𝐿(𝐷) is triangle-free.
Proof. An acyclic orientation of a triangle has vertices 𝑎, 𝑏, 𝑐 with edges 𝑎 → 𝑏, 𝑏 → 𝑐 and 𝑎 → 𝑐. If
𝑎 = (𝑢, 𝑣) and 𝑏 = (𝑣, 𝑤), the edge 𝑏 → 𝑐 makes the tail of 𝑐 equal to 𝑤, whereas 𝑎 → 𝑐 makes it equal
to 𝑣. Hence 𝑣 = 𝑤, contradicting the fact that 𝑏 is an arc of a simple graph. □

5. LEAN FORMALIZATION AND VERIFICATION
The accompanying file Erdos108.lean formalizes the construction and the two conclusions used
here. The theorem Bounty.paper_main asserts, for each 𝑀 ∈ N, the existence of a finite nonempty
simple graph that is triangle-free, has chromatic number at least 𝑀, and has every four-cycle-free
ordinary subgraph 6-colorable. The theorem Bounty.target proves the negation of the specified
Erdos108.erdos_108 type.
The formalization represents vertices of the multipartite model as pairs (𝑖, 𝑥) with 𝑖 < 𝐶 and 𝑥 < 𝑛 𝑖,
in lexicographic order. A sample is a finite dependent product of choices; unused choices into earlier
parts are retained so that the sample space is rectangular. Uniform probabilities are finite-set cardinalities
divided by the cardinality of the sample space. Thus the existence argument uses exact finite counting,
with real-valued estimates proved in Lean, rather than simulation or unverified numerical evaluation.
The graph-theoretic statements are formulated in terms of colorability. The predicate FourCycleFree
excludes two distinct vertices having two distinct common neighbors; in a simple graph this is exactly the
absence of an ordinary four-cycle. Subgraphs are handled through SimpleGraph.Subgraph, including
both vertex and edge deletions. The main correspondences are listed in Table 1.
The Lean proof establishes the 4-colorability conclusion of Theorem 3.1 directly by finite-set induc-
tion using the low-degree vertex supplied by the cut argument. No separate library definition of degen-
eracy is required. Remark 4.1 is a mathematical observation and is not a separate formalized assertion.
The library chromatic number takes values in the extended natural numbers. Its natural-valued girth
is zero for an acyclic graph, whereas we use infinite girth for forests in this paper. The proof only uses the
implication from library girth at least five to four-cycle-freeness. The stronger four-cycle-free conclusion
of Theorem 1.1 also covers forests, so this convention does not affect the counterexample. The final family
is transported by ULift to the arbitrary universe quantified over by the target statement.

6. CONCLUDING REMARKS
The obstruction is uniform: the bound six does not depend on the chromatic number of the host graph.
Hence the same family excludes a threshold for every girth parameter𝑟 ≥ 5 at chromatic parameter 𝑘 = 7.
The proof gives no claim that six is the smallest possible uniform bound.
The sizes in ( 4)–(5) were chosen to simplify the proof and its formalization. They specify a finite con-
struction, but are far too large to make enumeration of the required realizations practical. The conclusion
is an existence theorem; small computational examples are not used to certify the probability estimates.
